questions.q: Why is granting privileges to a group generally better than granting to individual users?
options: Onboarding and offboarding become a single group-membership change instead of separate GRANT/REVOKE pairs to track for each person
Groups run queries faster than individual users
Unity Catalog does not allow granting privileges to individual users at all
Group grants never need to be revoked
questions.explain: Granting to a group centralizes access management — adding or removing a person from the group handles access, instead of separate per-user grants accumulating as hard-to-audit exceptions.

questions.q: What does the principle of least privilege suggest when a team only needs access to one schema?
options: Grant at the schema level, not the whole catalog, even though inheritance would make a catalog-level grant also work
Always grant at the catalog level, since it's less work overall
Grant ALL PRIVILEGES on the metastore to be safe
Avoid granting schema-level access; only table-level grants satisfy least privilege
questions.explain: Because a catalog-level grant inherits down to everything inside it, least privilege means granting at the narrowest level that actually matches the need — the schema, not the broader catalog.

questions.q: What is the recommended approach to using the built-in account users group?
options: Use it sparingly, for genuinely public data — not as a default shortcut to avoid creating a proper group
Use it for every grant, since it's the simplest option
Never use it under any circumstances
It can only be used by metastore admins, never referenced in SQL
questions.explain: account users grants to literally everyone on the account; it's appropriate for genuinely public data but should not become a default way to avoid setting up a proper group.

questions.q: What is the benefit of running SHOW GRANTS proactively rather than only during an audit?
options: It catches stale grants — like one made months ago for a since-ended project that was never revoked
It automatically revokes all unused privileges
It is required before any GRANT statement will execute
It prevents service principals from ever being granted privileges
questions.explain: Periodically checking SHOW GRANTS surfaces grants that should have been revoked but weren't, rather than waiting until an external audit forces the review.

questions.q: A realistic access request for a new group member combines which elements from this chapter?
options: A principal, the usage-privilege chain (USE CATALOG/USE SCHEMA), an object-level privilege, and approval typically from the catalog/schema owner
Only a single GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES statement, nothing else
A principal and nothing else — privileges are automatic once a principal exists
Only a REVOKE statement, since new members start with full access by default
questions.explain: A realistic grant touches every concept in the chapter: a principal (Lesson 6) needs the usage-privilege chain (Lessons 7, 9) plus the specific object-level privilege, usually approved by an owner (Lesson 8).
